title: Post Acute Infectious Syndromes Interdisciplinary Care Berlin
summary: The PAIS CARE Study looks at how to improve care for people who still have symptoms weeks or months after an infection — such as COVID-19. This condition is called Post-Acute Infectious Syndrome (PAIS) and affects around 5–7% of people after COVID-19. Symptoms can be wide-ranging and persistent . The goal of this study is to collect data on patients' health, treatment, and quality of life. This will help understand what types of care work best. The study takes place in Berlin and involves patients from general practitioners (GPs). The results will be used to improve care for people with PAIS and to further develop effective healthcare services.

interventions.name: Individuals  suffering from post-acute infection syndrome are asked to answer several questionnaires regarding their medical, socioeconomic status and satisfaction with care (see primary and secondary outcomes for detailed information).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Triggering infection within the last 6 months prior to recruitment
‐ Development of lasting symptoms or complaints within 3 months after
the triggering infection
‐ Symptoms or functional limitations lasting for at least 2 months
‐ Patient is using Emails and can understand and answer informed
consent and online questionnaires in German language
‐ Patient able to give informed consent
‐ Signed informed consent by patient
Exclusion criteria:
- medical conditions that might interfere with the patient’s participation in
the study, poses any added risk for the patient, or confound the
assessment of the patient
‐ Known pregnancy
